newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba leaves key interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Buba leaves key interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its policy-making council had decided to leave the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The discount rate was kept steady at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also left unchanged at three percent.
Economists had generally agreed that a cut in the bank's leading interest rates was extremely unlikely.
"We certainly were not looking for anything on rates today," said Thomas Mayer, senior international economist at Goldman Sachs, after the news flashed across screens.
German shares were little changed at 2,905.12 on the announcement while Bund futures pared earlier gains to stand at 101.54, up nine basis points.
In a Reuter poll conducted this week, all 10 economists polled said they expected the discount and Lombard rates to remain unchanged.

Although soft October industrial output data fanned some speculation the Bundesbank might be tempted to nudge rates still lower in a bid to help economic growth, the Bundesbank reiterated recently that it sees no need to adjust rates now.

There had been some speculation in advance of the meeting that the central bank could decide to free private repo transactions from minimum reserve requirements at the meeting, but no statement has been made about that issue yet.
Shortly after the announcement that the central bank was leaving rates unchanged, a spokesman told Reuters that the policy-making council was continuing to meet.
A spokesman said the meeting was still going on at 1150 GMT, five minutes after the central bank said it was leaving its key interest rates unchanged.
